column1: # launch-check catalog. One row per check; tab-separated; "-" marks an empty cell (tab is IFS-whitespace, so cells are never empty).

# id | domain (security|tests-ci|tech-debt|reliability-ops) | class (readiness|baseline) | kind (presence|detector|judged) | title | severity (critical|high|medium|low) | stacks (any|node) | glob (|-separated, matched against the repo-relative path or any trailing path segment) | regex (ERE searched in matched files) | expect (present|absent) | closing command | remedy
# Baseline checks for the Soleur guards are NOT listed here: baseline.sh derives them from verification-scaffold/references/guards.tsv at run time.

column12: remedy
Remove the value and rotate the credential. This scan covers the last commit, not git history, so a secret removed from the current tree may still be live in history.
Untrack the file, add it to .gitignore, and rotate anything it held.
Commit a lockfile so installs are reproducible and auditable.
Enable Dependabot or Renovate so known-vulnerable dependencies are flagged.
Add CI that builds and tests every pull request.
Add tests for the paths customers depend on first: sign-in, payments, data writes.

column9: (npm|yarn|pnpm|bun)( run)? test|pytest|go test|cargo test|rspec|rake test|vitest|jest|phpunit|mvn( -B)? test|gradle test|dotnet test
column12: Make CI run the test suite and block merges when it fails.

column5: Deploy, release or rollback path documented or automated
column12: Write down, or automate, how a release goes out and how to roll it back.
Triage the markers: fix them, delete them, or turn the ones that matter into tracked issues.
Pin the runtime version so local, CI and production agree.

column5: Architecture notes or decision records present
column12: Record the main architecture decisions, one short file each, so they survive staff and context changes.
Add a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md so coding agents follow this repository's conventions.
Add the dependency-cruiser gate so client code cannot import server-only modules or secrets.
Add error tracking so production failures reach you before your customers do.
Expose a health endpoint that a monitor or load balancer can poll.
Document, or automate, backups and prove a restore works before launch.
Write short runbooks for the failures you expect: database down, bad deploy, expired credential.
Review how users sign in and which routes check permissions; close any route that trusts the client.

column5: Architecture, module boundaries and data layer
column12: Review module boundaries, migrations and destructive data operations; split or document what a new engineer could not safely change.

column5: Scaling hot spots and rate limiting
column12: Find the endpoints and queries that degrade first under load and add limits or caching before launch.
Make sure a failure at 3 a.m. is visible without logging into a server: logs, error tracking, uptime checks, alerts.
